key_insight: A basin-scale tracer flux balance links thermohaline circulation tipping to competing advective and dissipative transport, connecting box-model bifurcations to continuous ocean dynamics.
engineering_relevance: Separating transport contributions could improve ocean-model diagnostics of tipping risk beyond monitoring overturning strength alone.
method: Derive a tracer-conservation framework balancing surface fluxes with advection and dissipation.
Represent transport using large-scale tracer gradients and efficiency relative to a no-flow conductive state.
Evaluate transport regimes in a three-dimensional ocean-basin model and connect them to box-model limits.
evidence_signal: In the three-dimensional basin model, nonlinear salinity advection dominates the collapse threshold, while linear dissipation dominates recovery; transport scales approximately quadratically with weak circulation and linearly with strong circulation.
watch_item: Evidence here comes from an ocean-basin model; predictive flux-balance closures are deferred to Part II, so real-ocean tipping forecasts are not established.
paper_title: Basin-Scale Nonlinear Dynamics of Thermohaline Ocean Circulation. Part I: Theory
